_comment: The texts of the LabUtopia tasks, by family. `config` is LabUtopia's config for the task and `seed` the frozen instance's seed (make_facts.py); `level` is LabUtopia's own task level. `goal` is the privileged wording (the rule with its numbers, world frame); `goal_std` the standard wording, which never says where anything is in the world: every quantity is relative to where things start. `scene` and `inventory` describe what stands on the bench (names, sizes, colours; no positions). Sizes are bounding-box extents read from the scene.

pick.title: Pick
pick.goal: Pick up the conical flask that stands on the bench and hold it up. Success, at the first control step at which this has held for 60 consecutive control steps (1 s): the flask's centre is more than 0.10 m above where it started.
pick.goal_std: Pick up the glass conical flask that stands on the bench and hold it up. Success the moment the flask's centre has been more than 10 cm above where it stood for one second (60 control steps in a row).
pick.scene: On the bench in front of the arm: one glass conical (Erlenmeyer) flask, about 9.5 cm across at its base and 17 cm tall.
inventory: glass conical flask, about 9.5 cm across the base and 17 cm tall
pick.note: The flask is glass (nearly transparent in the cameras) and conical: the gripper closes on a wall that narrows upwards, and the flask has to stay in the grip for a full second 10 cm up.
pick.robot_text: a **Franka Panda** arm (7 joints) with its two-finger gripper, fixed to a laboratory bench

press.title: Press
press.goal: Press the red button on the instrument's front panel and keep it pressed. Success, at the first control step at which this has held for 60 consecutive control steps (1 s): the button's cap (`/World/target_button/button`) is beyond x = 0.405 m. It starts at x = 0.40 m and is pushed in along +x.
press.goal_std: Press the red button on the instrument's front panel (the two grey buttons next to it do not count) and keep it pressed. Success the moment its cap has been pushed in more than 5 mm for one second (60 control steps in a row). The panel is vertical and faces the arm: the button is pushed in along the forward (+x) axis of the arm's base.
press.scene: In front of the arm stands an instrument with a vertical front panel that carries three square buttons in a row, each 8 cm across: one red, two dark grey.
inventory: instrument with a vertical front panel
red square button, 8 cm across (the target)
two dark grey square buttons, 8 cm across
press.note: The target is one of three identical buttons told apart by colour only, on a vertical panel at arm's length; it has to be held in for a full second.
press.robot_text: a **Franka Panda** arm (7 joints) with its two-finger gripper, fixed to a laboratory bench

open_door.title: Open Door
open_door.goal: Open the door of the drying oven and let go of it. Success, at the first control step at which this has held for 60 consecutive control steps (1 s): the door handle's centre (`/World/DryingBox_01/handle`) is more than 0.12 m from where it started and the hand (the point between the fingertips) is more than 0.04 m from the handle's centre.
open_door.goal_std: Open the door of the drying oven and let go of it. Success the moment the door's handle has been more than 12 cm from where it started, with the gripper more than 4 cm away from the handle (measured from the point between the fingertips to the handle's centre), for one second (60 control steps in a row).
open_door.scene: On the bench in front of the arm: a drying oven, a grey metal box about 58 cm deep, 74 cm wide and 63 cm high, with a blue door that has a window and a handle and is hinged on one side; a small control panel sits next to the door. The door is closed.
inventory: drying oven (grey metal box, about 58 x 74 x 63 cm) with a blue hinged door with a window and a handle
control panel next to the door
open_door.note: A hinged door: the handle moves on an arc around the hinge, so the hand has to follow it, and the rule wants the door left open with the handle released.
open_door.robot_text: a **Franka Panda** arm (7 joints) with its two-finger gripper, fixed to a laboratory bench

open_drawer.title: Open Drawer
open_drawer.goal: Open the top drawer of the cabinet and let go of it. Success, at the first control step at which this has held for 60 consecutive control steps (1 s): the drawer handle's centre (`/World/Cabinet_01/drawer_handle_top`) is more than 0.12 m from where it started and the hand (the point between the fingertips) is more than 0.04 m from the handle's centre.
open_drawer.goal_std: Open the top drawer of the cabinet (the upper of its two drawers) and let go of it. Success the moment the drawer's handle has been more than 12 cm from where it started, with the gripper more than 4 cm away from the handle (measured from the point between the fingertips to the handle's centre), for one second (60 control steps in a row).
open_drawer.scene: On the bench in front of the arm: a grey cabinet with a white top, about 67 cm deep, 76 cm wide and 79 cm high: two drawers at the top, one above the other, each with a bar handle, and two doors below them. Everything is closed.
inventory: grey cabinet with a white top, about 67 x 76 x 79 cm
two drawers with bar handles (the upper one is the target)
open_drawer.note: The drawer has to be pulled out more than 12 cm by a thin bar handle and then released: a grip that slips leaves it short, and a drawer still held does not count.
open_drawer.robot_text: a **Franka Panda** arm (7 joints) with its two-finger gripper, fixed to a laboratory bench

place.title: Place (LabUtopia's level-2 TransportBeaker is the same task)
place.goal: Pick up the beaker and set it down on the square target plate. Success, at the first control step at which the second condition has held for 60 consecutive control steps (1 s): (1) the beaker's centre has been more than 0.10 m above where it started; (2) after that, its centre is within 0.05 m (horizontally) of the plate's centre and within 0.05 m of its initial height, and the hand (the point between the fingertips) is more than 0.05 m from the beaker's centre.
place.goal_std: Pick up the glass beaker and set it down on the white square plate. Success the moment, after the beaker's centre has been more than 10 cm above where it stood, the beaker has stood on the plate for one second (60 control steps in a row): its centre within 5 cm (horizontally) of the plate's centre and within 5 cm of the height at which it started, with the gripper more than 5 cm away from the beaker's centre (measured from the point between the fingertips).
place.scene: On the bench in front of the arm: a glass beaker, about 11 cm across and 9 cm tall, and a white square plate, 10 cm x 10 cm, lying flat on the bench.
inventory: glass beaker, about 11 cm across and 9 cm tall
white square target plate, 10 cm x 10 cm, flat
place.note: The beaker has to be lifted at least 10 cm, carried about half a metre and released upright within 5 cm of the centre of a 10 cm plate.
place.robot_text: a **Franka Panda** arm (7 joints) with its two-finger gripper, fixed to a laboratory bench

pour.title: Pour (LabUtopia's level-2 PourLiquid is the same task)
pour.goal: Pick up the small beaker, pour it out over the large beaker and bring it back upright. There is no liquid in this simulation: the pour is judged by where the small beaker is and how far it is turned. Success, at the first control step at which the last condition is met: (1) the small beaker's centre has been more than 0.12 m above where it started; then, counted only at control steps at which its centre is within the pour distance of the large beaker's centre (horizontally; half the height of the small beaker's bounding box plus 0.03 m, about 0.08 m), (2) it has been turned more than 50 degrees from its orientation at the first step after (1), (3) then turned back to within 30 degrees of that orientation, and (4) then is more than 0.05 m above where it started for 84 control steps (1.4 s).
pour.goal_std: Pick up the small glass beaker, pour it out over the large glass beaker and bring it back upright. There is no liquid in the simulation: the pour is judged by where the small beaker is and how far it is turned. Success the moment the last of these is met: (1) the small beaker's centre has been more than 12 cm above where it stood; then, counted only while its centre is within about 8 cm (horizontally) of the large beaker's centre, (2) it has been turned more than 50 degrees from its orientation right after (1), (3) then turned back to within 30 degrees of that orientation, and (4) then stays more than 5 cm above where it stood for 84 control steps (1.4 s).
pour.scene: On the bench in front of the arm: two glass beakers: a small one, about 11 cm across and 9.5 cm tall (the one to pour), and a large one, about 15.5 cm across and 13 cm tall (the one to pour into).
inventory: small glass beaker, about 11 cm across and 9.5 cm tall (the one to pour)
large glass beaker, about 15.5 cm across and 13 cm tall (the target)
pour.note: Four conditions in a fixed order, three of them counted only while the held beaker is within about 8 cm of the other one's axis: a tilt of more than 50 degrees and back, in the hand, without losing the beaker.
pour.robot_text: a **Franka Panda** arm (7 joints) with its two-finger gripper, fixed to a laboratory bench

shake.title: Shake (LabUtopia's level-2 ShakeBeaker is the same task)
shake.goal: Pick up the beaker, shake it, and hold it still. Nothing is counted at a control step at which the beaker's centre is less than 0.05 m above where it started. Success, at the first control step at which the second condition is met: (1) five times, the beaker's centre gets 0.05 m or more (horizontally) from where it was when that count began (each count begins at the next step); (2) after the fifth, its centre stays within 0.01 m in x and in y over 60 control steps (1 s).
shake.goal_std: Pick up the glass beaker, shake it, and hold it still. Nothing is counted while the beaker's centre is less than 5 cm above where it stood. Success the moment the second of these is met: (1) five times, the beaker's centre moves 5 cm or more (horizontally) from where it was when that count began; (2) after the fifth, the centre stays within 1 cm in each horizontal direction over one second (60 control steps in a row).
shake.scene: On the bench in front of the arm: one small glass beaker, about 6.5 cm across and 10 cm tall.
inventory: small glass beaker, about 6.5 cm across and 10 cm tall
shake.note: A small beaker has to survive five quick moves of 5 cm in the grip and then be held within 1 cm for a second: the grasp has to be firm enough for the accelerations.
shake.robot_text: a **Franka Panda** arm (7 joints) with its two-finger gripper, fixed to a laboratory bench

heat_liquid.title: HeatLiquid
heat_liquid.goal: Put the beaker on the heater's plate and press the heater's button. Success, at the first control step at which the third condition is met: (1) the beaker's centre has been above z = 0.82 m; (2) after that, the beaker has been on the plate: its centre at or below z = 0.86 m and within 0.05 m in x and in y of the plate's frame (`/World/heat_device/heat_device/heat_device/plat`); (3) after that, the beaker is on the plate as in (2) and the button's frame (`/World/heat_device/button`) is below z = 0.761 m.
heat_liquid.goal_std: Put the glass beaker on the heater's plate and press the heater's round red button. Success the moment the third of these is met: (1) the beaker's centre has been more than {lift_cm} cm above where it stood; (2) after that, the beaker has stood on the plate: its centre within 5 cm, in each horizontal direction, of the plate's centre and no more than {top_cm} cm above where it stood at the start; (3) after that, with the beaker on the plate as in (2), the button is pressed down more than {press_mm} mm.
heat_liquid.scene: On the bench in front of the arm: a small glass beaker, about 6.5 cm across and 10 cm tall, and a heater: a white hot plate about 25 cm x 18 cm x 9 cm with a square plate on top, a display on its front and a round red button at one front corner.
inventory: small glass beaker, about 6.5 cm across and 10 cm tall
heater (white hot plate, about 25 x 18 x 9 cm) with a square plate, a display and a round red button
heat_liquid.note: Two steps in order with one hand: the beaker has to stand within 5 cm of the plate's centre before the button, a few centimetres from the plate, is pressed down a centimetre without knocking the beaker off.
heat_liquid.robot_text: a **Franka Panda** arm (7 joints) with its two-finger gripper, fixed to a laboratory bench

open_close.title: OpenClose
open_close.goal: Open the top drawer of the cabinet, let go of it, then close it again and let go. Success, at the first control step at which the second condition has held for 60 consecutive control steps (1 s): (1) for 60 consecutive control steps, the drawer handle's centre (`/World/Cabinet_01/drawer_handle_top`) is more than 0.13 m from where it started and the hand (the point between the fingertips) is more than 0.04 m from the handle's centre; (2) after that, measured from where the handle was at the step (1) was met: the handle's centre is more than 0.13 m from there and nearer to where it started than it was at that step (the drawer has come back, not gone further out), and the hand is more than 0.04 m from the handle's centre.
open_close.goal_std: Open the top drawer of the cabinet (the upper of its two drawers), let go of it, then close it again and let go. Success the moment the second of these has held for one second (60 control steps in a row): (1) for one second, the drawer's handle is more than 13 cm from where it started, with the gripper more than 4 cm away from the handle (measured from the point between the fingertips to the handle's centre); (2) after that, the handle is more than 13 cm from where it was when (1) was met and nearer to where it started than it was then (pushed back, not pulled further out), again with the gripper more than 4 cm away.
open_close.scene: On the bench in front of the arm: a grey cabinet with a white top, about 67 cm deep, 76 cm wide and 79 cm high: two drawers at the top, one above the other, each with a bar handle, and two doors below them. Everything is closed.
inventory: grey cabinet with a white top, about 67 x 76 x 79 cm
two drawers with bar handles (the upper one is the target)
open_close.note: Two manipulations of the same drawer in a row, each ending with the handle released for a second: pull it out more than 13 cm, then push it back more than 13 cm.
open_close.robot_text: a **Franka Panda** arm (7 joints) with its two-finger gripper, fixed to a laboratory bench
